page.layout: One column of running text. No marginal notes. Catchword at the lower right, below the last line. Running head at the top, page number at the head.
page.running_head: De Agro Frisi. inter Lavic. & Amaf.

main_text.l: præter ea nihil se statutorum in societa-
tibus suis habere: præterea, si quæ so-
cietas civitati inutilis aut noxia videatur,
in potestate senatus esse, eam abroga-
re: item, si quis in societate quid com-
mittat, quo se indignum societate fecis-
se videatur, deque eo controversia exi-
stat, ejus cognitionem senatui deberi cum
tribus societatis præfectis: ad hæc, so-
cietates cum præfectis suis teneri, sum-
ma ope, summis viribus ut tueantur di-
gnitatem & jus senatus, eique auxilio &
firmamento sint, ac pœnas contumaci-
um, cum res requirit, promoveant. Ha-
bent tamen societatum præfecti in suâ
quisque societate potestatem cognoscen-
di controversias quasdam ad societatem
pertinentes, easque definiendi, ac mul-
tas quoque capiendi ab his, qui contra
societatis leges deliquisse deprehendun-
tur. Sed id totum sic habet, ut jurisdict-
ionis species aut pars videri nequeat.
Et si quis eo lædi se injuste à præfectis
existimet, is pro more Ædiles, tanquam
societatum summos magistros atque ἐφό-
ρους[?] appellat, ab his porrò, si placet, ad
ipsum

page.notes: Catchword "ipsum" is printed as "ipsutn"; the final letters are doubtful, hence [?]. The Greek word at the line end is printed "ἐφό-" with the continuation "ρυς" on the scan; read as ἐφόρους, marked [?]. The paragraph break before "Et si quis" is inferred from the sentence end and the flush-left line start; the line "nequeat." is near full width, so this break is not fully certain. The scan has a Google digitisation watermark at the lower right and a small mark at the bottom centre; both are excluded. "cum" in "cum res" appears to carry a faint mark above the u; read as plain cum.
